changelog: v352: answering a card places its moment. WHERE IT WAS SEEN: the owner's own vault, three times in two days, each time a "when did X happen?" card left open as if he had never answered. (1) `sources/conversations/msg-a2a65da9bda477a98f67f20c.md` — "This was mostly last month and he's stopped mostly now", captured 2026-09-24T01:09:30Z, `session_ref: conversation:cand:work_item:work:577ecc4639edf0f8ead752ca`, answering "When did Harvey's love of cussing happen?" (`node:3380558928426602253447c7`, subject `person/harvey`). Its classification holds `time_periods: [{era: "last month", approximate_dates: "2026-08"}]` and `events: []` — the TIME was read and no event was — so `classifier_claims` had nothing to hang it on, the general listener heard nothing, and NOTHING AT ALL was filed. (2) `msg-fc9845c47f8dc2b5099724a5.md` — "19-21 years old", answering the card about his father's mission: the listener filed `claim:65573521952535272873944a`, `claim_type: age`, 19–21, `subject_mention: "they"`, `event_kind: span`, NO `event_mention`, `confidence: 0.0`, which minted a node labelled `they` and a card "When was they?"; v343 suppresses that node and the ANSWER still never reached the moment it was about. (3) `msg-57c728860e184aaf2146b021.md` — "He only really started talking when he was 4", `claim:bf9f8a7a0faeb8bbb1ab77f1`, `claim_type: age`, 4, `subject_mention: "he"`, `event_mention: null`. THE CAUSE IS NOT A CARELESS MODEL. The reply carries the WHEN and the card carries the WHAT, and nothing joined them: every extractor that reads a promoted answer is shown the MESSAGE ALONE — the classify prompt (`classifier_context`, `contextual-timeline:3`) names no work item and `general_listener.build_listener_prompt` takes an answer and a reply and no question — so asked to find an event in "19-21 years old" an honest extractor either files nothing or files the time against whatever pronoun the sentence happens to carry. THE JOIN WAS ALREADY ON THE WIRE: `session_ref: conversation:cand:work_item:<id>` is on the frontmatter of every promoted message (the platform's own `conversation_source.promotion_metadata`, and the same string it hands `file-claims`), and the published `state/temporal_claims/work-items.json` carries that work item's `node_ref`, `subject_ref` and its own question. Nobody read it — v325's resolver revisit rung is the only thing in the repo that ever did, and that rung re-opens a MODEL question rather than filing the answer. THE RULE (`answer_placement.ANSWERING_A_CARD_PLACES_ITS_MOMENT`, the new `system/answer_placement.py`): a reply promoted with a `session_ref` naming a work item is read as an answer to THAT work item. The TIME it carries — a date, a range, an age, or a recency expression resolved against the message's own capture date — becomes a claim on the node the card is about, with the reply as its source and the record's basis `stated`, because the person is the one saying it. The SUBJECT comes from the NODE, never from a pronoun in the reply, which is the other half of v343's suppression: suppressing the bogus `they` node was right, and the answer must still land somewhere. And a reply carrying NO time at all still files as a TELLING of that node — an `occurrence`, which asserts that it happened and says nothing about when — so the card stays open with the owner's words on it and never silently nothing. NOTHING HERE IS A SECOND PARSER: the rungs are `chronology`'s own (`parse_stated_date`, `parse_age`, `from_recency` and its `RECENCY_RUNGS`) in the SAME order `classifier_claims.temporal_reading` reads them, and the confidences are that module's own constants (`AGE_CLAIM_CONFIDENCE`, `RECENCY_CLAIM_CONFIDENCE`, `OCCURRENCE_CLAIM_CONFIDENCE`, `landmark_projection.CONFIDENCE_SCORE`). The one thing added is `AGE_PHRASE_RES`, a CLOSED vocabulary of age phrasings built the way `RECENCY_RUNGS` is built, because `chronology.parse_age` is a FIELD parser and run over prose it reads "March 1998" as age 8 — `classifier_claims._age_band_text`'s own year trap, reused rather than re-decided, so a text naming a four-digit year DATES ITSELF and is never an age. A bare number behind "at" is refused outright (ADR 0026 ranks a miss above a wrong join, and "at 19 Elm Street" is already a named negative of the listener's own prescreen); "at about 4 years" still reads. FIVE NAMED REFUSALS, so a report says WHY instead of showing a smaller number: `card_not_published`, `card_not_open` (something else already settled it), `card_node_not_drawn`, `card_subject_unresolved` (Timeline Fix 01 P0b — when nobody knows WHICH James the row is about, no sentence can settle it) and `reply_has_no_words`. A DAY-SCOPED session (`…:work:<hex>:<YYYY-MM-DD>`, which the platform opens when a card's plain session has closed) names the SAME card: a second conversation about one question is not a second question, and `work_item_of_session` is now the ONE parse — `resolver._work_item_of_session` delegates to it rather than keeping a second copy that would not know that. TWO SEATS, ONE DERIVATION. `landmark_recorder.file_claims` already received the `session_ref` for its idempotency key, so it now AIMS every draft at the card before `bind_claims` sees it (`aim_at_card`: the draft's `event_ref` becomes the card's node, a bare PRONOUN subject becomes the node's own, an absent `event_mention` becomes the node's label) and, when the drafts assert no time at all — including the message that produced NO drafts, which used to file nothing — files the deterministic reading of the reply itself. A name the person actually used is never overwritten, the owner's own first person (`I`, `me`, `we`, `self`, `narrator`) is never rewritten because "I was 19" answering a card about somebody else's mission is the owner talking about himself, and `event_kind` is left exactly as it was heard. The second seat is `classifier_claims.migrate_classifier_moments`, the vault's one deterministic claim-filing sweep and the first step of the hosted daily sweep: a second rung that walks every promoted answer with a card whether or not any extractor heard anything in it, reported apart under its own `answers` block and described under its own heading, and it runs BEFORE the one rebuild and the one publish so the card an answer lands on is the card the person saw. `place-answers [--dry-run] [--json] [--source PATH]` is the same rung on its own verb, in `DIRECT_MUTATION_COMMANDS` beside `migrate-classifier-moments`. The receipt declares v337's own unit — `event_identity.conversation_telling_ref(<promoted source id>, <node hex>)`, one fact inside one message — so two answers to one card are two tellings of the SAME fact; the extractor version is its own (`answer-placement/rule:1`), never the listener's, because two readings of one message are two interpretations and a shared version would make them one claim that overwrote itself. `CALCULATION_RULE_VERSION` DOES NOT MOVE: this release adds CLAIMS and changes no derivation, so a vault nobody answered draws exactly what it drew and no golden moves. MEASURED on a scratch clone of the owner's vault (`/private/tmp/lifehug-rig-answer`, reset to the generation whose cards he was answering — `1daaeba3`, generation 118, all three cards open and all three nodes unplaced — with the three real promoted answers restored from the head and the v352 framework overlaid; the original was never written to). `place-answers` read 19 promoted answers carrying a card, PLACED 3, filed 3 as tellings and refused 13 as `card_not_published`. Open cards 48 -> 43 (precision_gap 43 -> 37, contradiction 5 -> 6), placed nodes 1188 -> 1193, node count unchanged at 1233, `node_aliases` 116 -> 118 and both new aliases published. "Harvey's love of cussing" is 2026-07-24/2026-09-24 basis `stated`, rendering "24 July 2026-24 September 2026 - you said last month, told 2026-09-24"; "Harvey's late talking start" is `2026~` basis `age`, measured from Harvey's own birth as that vault holds it (v346's `BIRTH_ANCHOR_TIERS`, tier 2, the roster row's `born: 2022`). The v340/v342 LOST-PLACEMENT AUDIT IS EMPTY — nothing lost, nothing moved to an incompatible date, nothing drawn at a redirected id. SIX precision-gap cards closed, three of them the owner's own, and ONE contradiction card appeared, which is v340 working: placing those moments collapsed a duplicate `James's birth` node, which armed v346's tier 1 for `person/james`, which made an EXISTING age-9 claim computable (`age_without_birth_anchor` became `age_contradicts_placement`, 1999-03-20/2000-03-19 against 1990-03-20) and the projection now asks "Two dates are claimed for James's birth — 20 March 1990 and around 1999. Which is right?" — a real disagreement in the owner's own statements, surfaced as a card he can answer. ONE THING THE RULE CANNOT FINISH, AND IT REPORTS IT BY NAME: "19-21 years old" now lands on `node:b69a5be503b14977a6ba0077` "Father's mission to New Zealand" as an `age` claim with the node's own subject — the answer REACHES its moment, which it never did before — and the fold cannot do the arithmetic, because that node's subject is the raw mention `James Edwin Taylor` and the owner's roster holds four people bearing the token James (`James Taylor` the father, born 1954-06-04 since v350's introduction; `James Edwin Taylor Sr.` the grandfather; `James` the brother; and the owner). v335's shared-name rule refuses an ambiguous key and is right to, so the fold reports `age_without_birth_anchor` on the claim and the projection raises "Which James or James Edwin Taylor Sr. or James Taylor is 'James' here?" as an `identity_uncertain` card. Placing that span is an IDENTITY question and not a dating one; it is the next defect rather than this one, and the synthetic fixture pins the arithmetic that answers it the moment identity does (19–21 from 1954-06-04 is 1973-06-04/1976-06-03). GUARDS: `tests/test_v352_answering_a_card_places_its_moment.py` — all three of the owner's real shapes as fixtures on a synthetic vault whose cards are minted by the REAL minter (`temporal_publication.publish`), so the question, the node and the subject are the ones on his vault rather than hand-written. The defect REPRODUCED first (three promoted answers in the vault and three cards still asking), then all three placing, the three cards closing, no node labelled with a pronoun, the claim's subject proved to be the node's, the reply proved to be the claim's own source at that reply's own content revision, the v340/v342 placement audit empty over the whole act, idempotency (a second run writes no receipt and derives the same claim ids), determinism over repeated runs, a dry run writing nothing, a restricted run touching one answer; the reading ladder over the owner's words and over a date, a range and an approximate year, the year trap closed in both directions, "at 30 Elm Street" refused, every age phrasing the vocabulary holds, a recency cue read against the CARD's own question and bounding nothing without a capture date; the join including the day-scoped session and the resolver's delegation to it; all five refusals; aiming a draft (the pronoun replaced, a name never overwritten, an event never overwritten, the kind untouched, the owner's first person never rewritten); the listener seat end to end (the `they` draft placing the card and minting no `they` node, a message with no drafts placing its card, a message with no drafts and no card still filing nothing, one utterance staying one promoted source); the sweep carrying the rung, dry and wet, described apart; the receipt's declared telling ref and its own extractor version; cards by kind before and after; and `CALCULATION_RULE_VERSION` proved not to move. Full local suite: 6767 tests, 6762 passed, 1 failed (the known macOS-only `test_file_answer_outer_queue_leaves_no_plaintext_temp`), 4 skipped, and the checkout clean afterwards. Ruff parity held exactly: `classifier_claims.py`, `landmark_recorder.py`, `resolver.py` and `lifehug.py` match their v351 finding CLASSES with nothing new on either side (the RUF100 `PLC0415` count grows by exactly the lazy imports added, which is each file's own convention), and `answer_placement.py` carries only the two classes every sibling module carries.
